_rationale: Cash branch in growth loop must take precedence over allocation lookup. With stockAllocation=0.6 misconfigured, a naive `balances[id] *= sa*sf + (1-sa)*bf` would compute 1.34× growth → $134k pre-spending → $114k after $20k spending. The correct bypass: cash grows by (1 + cashYieldRate) = 1.04 → $104k pre-spending. cashInterest ($4k) is ordinary income and contributes to availableCash, so the principal withdrawal is only $16k (= $20k spending − $4k interest income). End-of-year cash = $104k − $16k = $88k. Probability = 100% (cash doesn't deplete in 6 years).

pathValues.note: Year 1 start = year 0 end = (100k × 1.04 yield) - 16k principal withdrawal = $88k. If bypass missing, would be ~$114k.

breakdownChecks._note: $20k spending need − $4k cash interest income = $16k principal pull
